summary: Frontend-only regression for mobile dashboard scroll-perf fix. Logged in as Firebase test user on 390x844 viewport, verified all mobile testids (dash-mobile-header, dash-mascot, open-tools-btn, dashboard-light-zone, tier-plan-card, dashboard-quota, bottom-nav, mobile-avatar-btn), measured FPS during rAF-driven oscillating scroll (0..1000px, 1.8s) and confirmed interactions (profile-sheet open + drag-to-dismiss, tools ring open/close). Also verified body background CSS switches (scroll on mobile, fixed on desktop) and home page mobile.

perf_measurements.verdict: PASS - both exceed thresholds by wide margin (was ~22 fps before fix)

verifications.visual_background: dark cosmic purple confirmed (bg color lab(3.52 1.49 -8.61)), no white/blank body

observations: mascot src attribute not directly readable via get_attribute on the wrapper (returned None) — element itself is visible and rendered correctly per screenshot. Not a bug, selector nuance only.

Desktop reload landed on the Analyze/pair-picker view rather than the hero (URL still /dashboard). The desktop hero testids (dash-desktop-hero, desktop-open-tools-btn, desktop-copy-email) were not visible, but this is a route-state artefact after reload (likely last-tab persistence via localStorage), not a regression caused by the perf fix. Screenshot confirms desktop renders fine with dark background and header.
critical_code_review_comments: Perf fix is effective and safe: mobile body background switches to background-attachment:scroll, desktop keeps fixed. FPS restored to ~60 even under 4x CPU throttling.
Optional follow-up: if desktop hero should be the default on /dashboard load, verify the tab-state persistence logic in the desktop layout.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Mobile scroll perf fix verified at 60 fps (normal + 4x CPU throttle). All mobile dashboard testids present. Profile sheet drag-dismiss and tools ring open/close work. Desktop bg-attachment:fixed retained. Only observation: desktop /dashboard after reload showed Analyze pair-picker rather than hero — investigate tab-state persistence if that's unintended.
